account:
Today I have followed my appointments: correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, and now tea with my neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage. The treasury contained 128 emeralds when I checked it, and I left those funds untouched. I am due back in the office at 16:30.

The unusual business is the builder and Freight shouting earlier today. The secretary heard them too but could not make out their words. I have not heard enough to know what their exchange concerned. The secretary offered to investigate and has now reported that the builder wants approval for a great hall lighting and table inspection tomorrow at 18:00. I approved that and asked for it to be entered in my appointments, although the secretary has just asked for confirmation again. The secretary has not yet reached Freight. I cannot establish whether the inspection request is connected to the shouting.

I also noticed a block in the great hall at (-58, -60, 26) change from air to oak planks around 13:17. I did not see who placed it or learn its purpose. It might concern hall work, but that is only a possibility.

Townsfolk have repeatedly reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and later a sack of bread at the inn and near the plaza. Those reports suggest bread preparation and transport, but I have no direct evidence of anything improper or of a connection to the builder and Freight.

My neighbour has welcomed me for tea and says the docks are peaceful, with no fresh or pressing news. For now, the outstanding matters are confirming the inspection appointment and learning what Freight has to say, rather than assuming there is a problem.
